---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 3.1: compile the Bayesian models (pathologists)"
---

Step 3.1 of the paper simulation (pathologist design): compile the brms model once (cmdstanr, no
sampling). The fitting step refits the template on every dataset with `update(recompile = FALSE)`.

**Model** (slide and rater effects, every rater scores every slide): binomial + Poisson,
TP ~ Bin(P, recall), FP ~ Poisson, independent slide effects, rater effects correlated between the
parts (skill and cutoff move recall and FP together).

- brms default priors, except the intercept of the FP part: student_t(3, 1, 2.5) on log FP, as in
  step 3 (the brms default depends on the compile data).

**Compile data:** scenario C, 40 slides, rep 1, variant 1 (data example). Stan does not fix the data
dimensions at compile time, so one template fits both variants (23 and 9 raters).

**Output** (`simulation/models/`)

- The executables of the models (ignored by git, rebuilt by this step).
- `03_1_brms_templates_pathologists.rds`: named list of the compiled templates.
- `03_1_model_versions.csv`: R, brms, cmdstanr and CmdStan versions and the compile data.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(brms)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# Columns for the binomial + Poisson model
prepare_brms_data <- function(df_sim) {
  df_sim |>
    mutate(GroundTruth = TP + FN)    # Sensitivity/recall trials: all true objects (P)
}
```

# Load data
```{r}
df_counts <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_1_pathologist_observed_data.csv.xz")

df_compile <- df_counts |>
  filter(scenario == "C", rep == 1, variant == 1) |>
  prepare_brms_data()
```

# Models
```{r}
# Binomial + Poisson: TP ~ Bin(P, recall), FP ~ Poisson(mu) independent of TP,
# independent slide effects, correlated rater effects (shared label r)
bf_pois_tp <- bf(TP | trials(GroundTruth) ~ 1 + (1|slide) + (1|r|rater_ID), family = binomial())
bf_pois_fp <- bf(FP ~ 1 + (1|slide) + (1|r|rater_ID), family = poisson())

model_formulas <- list(
  "Binomial + Poisson" = bf_pois_tp + bf_pois_fp
)

# Fixed intercept prior of the FP part (the brms default depends on the data);
# all other priors are brms defaults
model_priors <- list(
  "Binomial + Poisson" = prior(student_t(3, 1, 2.5), class = Intercept, resp = FP)
)
```

# Compile
```{r}
dir_models <- "simulation/models"
dir.create(dir_models, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Compile once without sampling (chains = 0). The executables go into dir_models
# (absolute path, so they are found from any working directory).
# With cmdstanr, chains = 0 still runs 1 chain with 1 iteration, hence the
# divergence and E-BFMI warnings.
brms_templates <- imap(model_formulas, \(formula, model)
  brm(formula, data = df_compile, prior = model_priors[[model]],
      backend = "cmdstanr", chains = 0, refresh = 0,
      stan_model_args = list(dir = normalizePath(dir_models)))
)
```

# Save
```{r}
saveRDS(brms_templates, file.path(dir_models, "03_1_brms_templates_pathologists.rds"))

tibble(
  r_version        = R.version.string,
  brms             = as.character(packageVersion("brms")),
  cmdstanr         = as.character(packageVersion("cmdstanr")),
  cmdstan          = cmdstanr::cmdstan_version(),
  compile_scenario = "C",
  compile_n_slide  = 40,
  compile_rep      = 1,
  compile_variant  = 1,
  created          = format(Sys.time())
) |>
  write_csv(file.path(dir_models, "03_1_model_versions.csv"))
```

# Load
```{r}
# Saved templates: the check also runs without compiling again
brms_templates <- readRDS("simulation/models/03_1_brms_templates_pathologists.rds")
```

# Check: default priors of another dataset
```{r}
# update(recompile = FALSE) reuses the compiled executable, so every fit uses the priors of the
# template. Compare for a very different dataset (scenario A, variant 2):
#   template = priors of the template (compile data)
#   default  = default priors brms would choose for df_check
df_check <- df_counts |>
  filter(scenario == "A", rep == 1, variant == 2) |>
  prepare_brms_data()

df_prior_check <- imap(brms_templates, \(template, model) {
  list(
    template = prior_summary(template),
    default  = default_prior(formula(template), data = df_check)
  ) |>
    map(\(priors) as_tibble(priors) |> select(prior, class, coef, group, resp, dpar)) |>
    bind_rows(.id = "source_prior") |>
    mutate(model = model)
}) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = source_prior, values_from = prior)

# Priors that differ between the template and the defaults for df_check
# (expected: only the fixed FP intercept prior)
df_prior_check |>
  filter(template != default) |>
  select(model, class, resp, dpar, group, template, default)

# All priors of the templates
df_prior_check |>
  select(model, class, resp, group, coef, template) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```
